summary: Guard Dog M1 backend+frontend fully validated against the live public URL. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass covering /api/health (provider.configured=false), /api/config (rulesetId, controlledEndpoint, capabilities), /api/rules/{id}/latest with INDEPENDENT Ed25519 signature verification over RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256 payloadHash parity check using public key from /api/keys, /api/rules/unknown/latest -> 404, /api/rules/{id}/versions (no MongoDB _id leaked), /api/rules/sign 401 without admin token / 200 with token / host canonicalization ('Evil.Example.' -> 'evil.example') / bundleVersion increment / 422 RULE_CONFLICT on a.example block vs A.EXAMPLE. allow, /api/keys with publicKeyB64 and no private material, /api/intelligence/lookup: mixed-case controlled host -> verdict=block, source=local-signed-rules, sanitizedUrl 'https://m1-block-test.guarddog.example/x' (query stripped), unknown host -> verdict=unknown, degraded=true, source=none (fail-open, not block), javascript: URL -> 422. Frontend (Expo web preview, viewport 390x844): harness-screen loads with no red screen; config-ruleset, config-host, config-ipv4, bundle-version all populated from backend; protection-state-badge=INACTIVE; default analyze produces analysis-sanitized-url 'https://m1-block-test.guarddog.example/login' and analysis-verdict containing 'block'; invalid URL ('not a url') surfaces analysis-invalid; run-proof-button yields the honest step sequence: config PASS, bundle PASS, verify BLOCKED, before BLOCKED, consent BLOCKED, start SKIPPED with harness-verdict 'Proof incomplete: requires Android native build + real controlled endpoint.'; no [data-testid="event-THREAT_BLOCKED"] node exists; blocked-count is 0. Mocked provider correctly detected: Google Web Risk is unconfigured (provider.configured=false) and unresolved lookups return unknown/degraded=true.
critical_code_review_comments: Admin sign endpoint has no guard preventing operators from replacing the controlled-endpoint bundle with an unrelated rule set, which effectively 'demotes' the M1 controlled-block bundle from 'latest'. Consider (a) making the seeded controlled rule a floor that admin-signed bundles must include, or (b) exposing a distinct rulesetId for admin experimentation so gd-m1-controlled-block cannot be replaced accidentally. This was observed as an ergonomic footgun during testing (integration tests now restore the bundle at teardown).
seed_data_creation: No seed data was persisted beyond bundle-version bumps. The sign test resigns a restore-controlled rule for host m1-block-test.guarddog.example at teardown so /api/rules/gd-m1-controlled-block/latest continues to match the harness expectations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL: https://guard-dog-m1.preview.emergentagent.com. Admin header: X-GuardDog-Admin-Token: m1-dev-admin-token-change-me. Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_m1_endpoints_integration.py -v. Includes independent Ed25519+JCS+SHA-256 signature verification via cryptography.ed25519 (no dependency on backend internals). If a follow-up frontend test needs the default URL to yield 'block', ensure the last admin-signed bundle for gd-m1-controlled-block still contains a rule with host m1-block-test.guarddog.example (the sign test's teardown handles this).
rca_of_issue: One transient false negative was observed on first run: the default frontend URL yielded verdict=unknown instead of block. Root cause: the pytest sign-canonicalization test replaced /api/rules/gd-m1-controlled-block/latest with a bundle whose only rule targeted host 'evil.example'. Because index.tsx calls GuardDogSecuritySDK.acceptRuleBundle(bundle.data) on the LATEST bundle (shape-only on web) and analyzeUrl performs an exact-host match against payload.rules, the controlled host was no longer present so 'unknown' was the correct honest answer. Mitigation: the sign test now performs a second signing call at teardown that reinstates a rule for host m1-block-test.guarddog.example, restoring the controlled bundle. Re-run confirmed verdict='block (restore-controlled)'. This is a test-isolation concern, not a product defect.
